previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for severe neck and throat pain, tachycardia, and a productive cough, in the setting of ongoing treatment for tracheal squamous cell carcinoma. She was found to have candidal esophagitis, likely exacerbated by recent radiation and chemotherapy, contributing to dysphagia and pain. A bloodstream infection due to her central venous catheter was identified, with Staphylococcus isolated from blood cultures, prompting antibiotic therapy and PICC line replacement. She also had acute bronchitis and chronic obstructive asthma exacerbation, though imaging showed no pneumonia. Malnutrition and edema were managed with TPN and nutritional support. Her tachycardia improved with metoprolol. Over the 12-day admission, she transitioned from TPN to oral intake, completed antibiotic treatment, and showed clinical improvement. She was discharged home with home health services, a revised medication plan, and follow-up with oncology.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Staphylococcus infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site, other staphylococcus

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ with a history of chronic pain, fibromyalgia, 
likely radiation esophagitis from recent treatment of ___ of 
trachea presenting with nausea, diarrhea, and atypical chest 
pain.  

1) Atypical Chest Pain: Patient presented with persistent, 
nonexertional left chest and shoulder pressure that was not 
associated with shortness of breath or diaphoresis.  This 
persisted over her first night in the hospital but ECG remained 
unchanged from baseline and patient ruled out with two sets of 
cardiac biomarkers.  Ultimate etiology of pain felt quite 
unlikely to be cardiac but given multiple presentations with 
atypical pain complaints, associated nausea, persistence, and 
risk factors for CAD (smoking, chronic inflammatory 
condition)decision was made to proceed to stress test with 
inpatient chosen given patient's history of imperfect follow up. 
Persantine stress deferred due to bronchospasm but pt felt 
unable to exercise given musculoskeletal issues so nuclear 
dobutamine test obtained and was essentially normal.  Her pain 
resolved on its own.  The likely etiology of her pain was felt 
to be referred pain from her MSK complaints vs from post 
radiation changes in her throat and upper chest. 

 
2) Diarrhea with incontinence/ constipation: Pt reported 
diarrhea and plan was made for infectious work up with stool 
studies but despite account of diarrhea patient did not have a 
bowel movement while in the hospital and as of hospital day two 
she began to complain of constipation and was given a bowel 
regimen.  No bowel movement but abdomen was soft and minimal 
tenderness with good bowel sounds so it was not felt this needed 
to hold discharge.  Likely etiology of constipation and diarrhea 
is opiate induced constipation with overflow or laxative induced 
diarrhea.  Also some possibility of viral gastroenteritis given 
reported nausea/vomiting as well.   

3) Nausea: Pt reported nausea prior to admission but never had 
this or vomiting in house.  Etiology unclear though some 
suspicion of viral gastroenteritis though continued problems 
with radiation esophagitis.  

4) Dehydration: Pt appeared dehydrated at presentation and 
received IVF.  At the time of discharge was tolerating full diet 
and did not appear dehydrated.  

5) Sore throat: Pt with persistent sore throat since her 
chemoRT.  Diagnostic EGD on ___ showed no fungal forms or 
viral inclusion bodies.  This is a chronic problem and patient 
ate relatively well during hospitalization.  She was continued 
on her H2 blocker. 

6) Lower extremity paresthesias: Pt reported paresthesias of 
shins and feet with pins and needles sensation, burning, and 
diminished sensitivity to light touch.  In stocking distribution 
consistent with peripheral neuropathy possibly related to recent 
taxane treatment.  She will discuss this with her oncologists.

7) Anemia: Likely anemia of chronic inflammation given recent 
cancer treatment and multiple stressors.  Her Hct fell during 
her hospitalization but this was in the context of hydration and 
Hct of 24.9 near previous baseline.  She never had signs of 
acute bleeding in house. 

8) Mixed connective tissue disorder: Stable, she was continued 
on her home prednisone.

9) Chronic pain: She continued her morphine SR and oxycodone at 
home doses.  

She was kept on subcutaneous heparin for DVT prophylaxis.  She 
tolerated a full diet prior to discharge.  She was full code

vomiting.  Your nausea and diarrhea resolved on their own and we 
suspect they were due to a viral illness that has resolved.  
Your labs and tests did not suggest a life threatening or severe

on to a test to look for significant blockages in your heart, 
which was negative.  Likely your pain is referred from your

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___ and a CTA chest from

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Chest pain, question pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  Evaluation is
limited given the low lung volumes.  Allowing for this, lungs appear clear
bilaterally.  Linear densities in the mid lungs are likely related to small
amount of scarring as seen previously on chest CT.  There is mild prominence
of the left pulmonary hilum, which is likely related to prominent vascular
structures.  No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  Bilateral
shoulder replacements are present.  Vascular calcification along the thoracic
aorta at the level of the knob noted.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic process.
